author: cerebral_barrier
text_post: I'm getting older and with my only successful foray into DSR 3 years behind me, I've called it quits on women and I'm looking for new adventures to keep me sane.  I've been doing all kinds of cool manly stuff lately; working on my house, building furniture (from scratch), working on cars, spending waaaaay too much time playing video games and practicing my latent (ex-military) marksmanship abilities at the local gun range. So about a week ago, I visited the local range with a close friend.  There was nothing new or special going on that day; just two guys out to have fun.   My friend and I were taking turns practicing our aim; firing at targets and having a good time.  When you go to the gun range, there should always be a strong emphasis on firearm safety and situational awareness and this day was no different.  You can pretty much size up every shooter you see; assessing their skill level, admiring the bad asses with their pin point accuracy and making note of anyone who may pose a safety hazard.   Sometimes, you'll see couples come in with one spouse teaching the other how to shoot.   I made note of the couple in the lane next to us; nothing out of the ordinary.   The guy's wife was struggling to manage the recoil of her gun.   It was kind of comical to watch; sort of like a 3 year old trying to control a pitt bull on its leash.  As cringe worthy as it was to watch, at least her bullets were still hitting the paper when she shot.   So my friend and I were taking turns; one of us shooting, the other one watching the other nearby lanes in case anything happened.   ...and it's a good thing we were.   During my turn to shoot, I feel myself violently yanked backward by my shoulder.   My friend had pulled me about a foot backward from my shooting position.   I suppose most people would be like "WTF are you doing?" but my friend and I are both gun range safety nuts so I knew something was up.   Turns out, the woman next to us jammed her gun, then she and her husband (both with their hands on the gun at the same time) tried to clear the jam.   At some point the weapon's slide snapped forward into the firing position; chambering a round.  My friend was watching the whole scenario unfold and made the decision to pull me backward.   Before he did this, the woman's gun was pointed in my direction with a live round in the chamber and her finger on the trigger. Make friends, people.  Make real friends.   Get the fuck off social media and get to know people in the real world.  As you can see, it may quite literally save your life.
